column1: # CONFORMANCE TABLE -- c2's inline decision function, clause by clause.
# Lane w-inlmetric. Source: docs/whitebox/ref/P_INLINE.md SS1-SS2 +
# docs/whitebox/WB_INLINE_FINDINGS.md SS1-SS2.4. Frozen by work/w-inlmetric/PREREG.md SS1.
# ADDRESS REPAIR, lane w-clausefix 2026-08-28, under work/w-clausefix/PREREG.md.
# TEN of the 24 `addr` cells did not name the instruction their `clause` names:
#   C2 C3 C4 C14 C16 C17 C18 C19  -- mid-instruction, found by the ALIGN check
#   C10 C15                       -- ALIGNED, in the right function, WRONG
#                                    instruction; no alignment check can see
#                                    this class, which is why `asm` exists.
# Only the `addr` column moved, plus the additive `asm` column. No clause, owner,
# state, witness, exercised or note cell was touched, and the split is unchanged
# at absent 17 / fitted 2 / R-derived 2 / unexercisable 3 over 24 rows
# (reachable denominator 21).
# THIS IS A PROGRESS INSTRUMENT, NEVER A GATE (docs/FUNCTION_BYTE_MATCH.md SS0).
# It licenses no emit. Nothing here enters crates/.
# addr        the c2 VA the clause is read at, in c2.dll sha256 c80981c0..a66258.
#             MECHANICALLY CHECKED by work/w-inlmetric/check_table.py, three ways:
#             (1) ADDRESS -- inside the FUNCS.tsv extent of `owner`;
#             (2) ALIGN   -- starts an instruction, per the INDEPENDENT objdump
#                            listing (not the Ghidra database the addrs came from);
#             (3) DECODE  -- the instruction there is the one `asm` records.
# owner       the function the page claims the addr is in. A mismatch is RED.
# asm         the objdump `-M intel` text at `addr`, runs of blanks collapsed.
#             It PINS THE ADDRESS TO A DECODE. It does NOT verify the clause --
#             for the four rows whose clause cites a function ENTRY (C1, C5/C6,
#             C20, C21) the witness is `push ebp`, which is weak ON PURPOSE and
#             is recorded here so nobody reads DECODE-GREEN as clause-confirmed.
# state       R-derived | fitted | absent | unexercisable
#               R-derived     the port's counterpart is derived from the same
#                             field/fact c2 tests, with a DISCLOSURE-grade trail.
#               fitted        a counterpart exists and is a black-box FIT, not
#                             a reading of this clause.
#               absent        no counterpart in crates/. Ties break HERE (PREREG SS5).
#               unexercisable no compilation this project runs can reach the
#                             clause, so `absent` would mis-read it.
# witness     path:token  (verified present)  |  none:<token-that-must-be-ABSENT>
# exercised   yes | no | not-separable | unexercisable  -- by the 878-TU workload,
#             measured on the 100-TU hold-out's 8,936 graded callees where possible.
# READ COLUMNS, lane w-inlclause 2026-08-29, under work/w-inlclause/PREREG.md.
# Board #3796-#3801. Graded by work/w-inlclause/read_state.py.
# `state` says whether the PORT has a counterpart. It says nothing about
# whether THIS PROJECT has read the clause well enough to build one, and on
# 2026-08-29 all fifteen `absent` rows were carrying one word for two
# situations a reader would act on differently:
#     "nobody has read this"                   -> a read is the next step
#     "it is read and the port cannot use it"  -> a read buys nothing
# THE ANSWER IS 13 UNADOPTED TO 2 UNREAD, not the large unread column the
# word `absent` suggests. Measured by work/w-inlclause/read_scan.py, which
# greps a frozen corpus of PROSE reads for the addresses that PIN each clause
# -- which for eight of the fifteen is NOT the address the row cites.
# read        R1 | R2 | R3, orthogonal to `state`.
#               R1  READ AND DERIVABLE. An address-cited read exists from
#                   which a port counterpart could be written today with every
#                   field carrying a PROV[R] address.
#               R2  READ, NOT DERIVABLE. A read exists and a NAMED link
#                   between c2's quantity and anything crates/ can compute is
#                   missing. `blocker` names it.
#               R3  UNREAD. Nothing in the corpus reads the clause beyond
#                   restating it. R3 is NOT CHEAP: a universal negative over a
#                   corpus is the easiest thing here to assert and the hardest
#                   to check, so every R3 row owes a recorded search in
#                   work/w-inlclause/UNREAD_EVIDENCE.md.
#             Ties break AWAY from R1 -- it is the only value that licenses an
#             adoption. THERE ARE NO R3 ROWS ON THIS TREE; C5 and C6 were the
#             two, and w-inlclause read them (IMAGE_READ.md SS3-SS4).
# readcite    path#anchor. The path must exist and the anchor must be present
#             in it. `-` only for R3.
# blocker     R1: none (adoptable) | emit-change (derivable, out of a
#             byte-neutral lane's scope).   R2: the missing link, and FOUR of
#             the six R2 rows name the SAME one -- `no-instr-count`, the port
#             has no pre-codegen instruction count. That is one missing link,
#             not six reasons.   unexercisable rows: n-a.
# THE SPLIT MOVED, absent 15 -> 12 / R-derived 4 -> 7, and only two of the
# three moves were conversions in the usual sense:
#   C14, C18   STALE. The port has carried counterparts since w-inlbudget
#              (2026-08-28) -- INLINE_LEVEL_DEPTH_CAP and
#              INLINE_CHARGE_EXEMPT_MAX, both PROV[R] at these rows' own
#              addresses, and that rung names C14 and C18 in those words. The
#              rows stayed `absent` because the ABSENCE screen checks ONE
#              SPELLING: it is a NAME screen in the direction #3641 declares
#              (a mention read as a counterpart) AND in the direction nobody
#              had declared -- A COUNTERPART ADOPTED UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME IS
#              INVISIBLE TO IT. C3 and C19 only converted last wave because
#              the adopting lane happened to choose colliding tokens.
#   C15        A real adoption, w-inlclause, byte-neutral by construction.
